QF.id: XIII Trading, Clearing, Settlement and Risk Management_29

question.text: A stock's Market Wide Position Limit (MWPL) is 1,00,00,000 shares (1 crore). The current aggregate open interest across all exchanges is 96,00,000 shares. What trading restriction applies?

answer.text: The stock enters a ban period since aggregate OI (96%) exceeds 95% of MWPL; only offsetting (square-off) trades are permitted
No restriction — the ban triggers only when OI reaches 100% of MWPL
New positions are restricted only for the exchange where OI is highest, not across all exchanges
The stock enters risk reduction mode where margins are increased by 50%, but new positions are still allowed

explanation.text: The Logic: When aggregate open interest across all exchanges reaches or exceeds 95% of MWPL, the stock enters a ban period. At 96,00,000 / 1,00,00,000 = 96%, which exceeds 95%, the ban is triggered. Only offsetting/square-off positions are allowed; no fresh positions. The ban is lifted once aggregate OI falls below 80% of MWPL. The Trap: The ban threshold is 95% of MWPL, not 100%. The ban is market-wide (across ALL exchanges), not exchange-specific. Note the asymmetric thresholds: 95% to enter the ban, 80% to exit. Note: Members who take fresh positions during the ban period are liable to penalties prescribed by the exchange. The exact penalty rates are notified by the exchange/SEBI and are not stated as a specific percentage in the workbook reference for this item.
